setting: You are all in the Lake District, England, where you live in and around Keswick, a short drive from each other. You are close friends who met through mutual friends and see each other most weekends. Cat Bells is a fell above Derwentwater near Keswick that is open to walkers all year, with no gates or seasonal closures.

Leah.who: 34, woman, a friend planning the walk
Leah.knows: You know Ravi and Freya as close friends from years of weekend walks and nights out, and you are the one usually organising the group's outings.
Leah.texts: You message in the group now and then, mostly when you have a plan to suggest.
Leah.style: Moderate emoji and light texting abbreviations.

Ravi.knows: You know Leah and Freya as close friends you have walked with for years, and Leah is the one who usually puts the plans together.

private_lines.Leah: You work as a nurse on rotating shifts at the hospital in Carlisle, which is about an hour's drive from home. You live alone in a small terraced house in Keswick, and your days vary with your rota, so you often get your days off in the middle of the week.
private_lines.Ravi: You run your own electrical business, taking jobs around Keswick and the surrounding valleys, so your days start early and finish when the jobs are done. You live alone in a flat above a shop in Keswick, and most weekends you are free to get out on the fells.
private_lines.Freya: You work as a research scientist at a lab on the edge of Keswick, where your days are mostly lab work and writing up results at a desk. You live alone in a cottage on the edge of town, and you spend a lot of your free time walking the local fells.

topic: Is the Cat Bells walk in the Lake District open all year, and how long does the main route take?

text: Right so cat bells for sunday? Is it still open all year or does it close for anything. And roughly how long is the main route
Open all year, no gates or closures. I did it in feb. Main route from hawse end is about 2.5-3hrs return depending how long you sit at the top
[photo: the ridge from hawse end, grey sky]
can do sunday. might have a job in borrowdale till 1 though
9 is early for you isn't it ravi
🙌 sorted then. Parking at hawse end is pay and display right? Anyone know if it's full by 9
Never full at 9. Busy by 11 easily tho
Bring layers, it'll be windy on the top
I'm on a late shift tomorrow no wait off sunday sorry. Pub after sounds good
[photo: sunset over derwent from the cottage step]
Bit tired already. I'll see you both at hawse end, don't be late 😂
I won't be late. Sleeping on this is impossible though, the forecast says 40mph gusts on the top
